slides.title: Woke up at 3 AM wanting p*rn? [[Here's what to do in the next 3 minutes.]]
slides.sub: Half-asleep is when your guard is lowest.

slides.title: Don't [[check the time]]
slides.body: Reaching for your phone "just to see the time" is how many 3 AM p*rn sessions start. Keep your hands off it.

slides.title: Get [[cold]]
slides.body: Kick off the covers for a minute. Splash water on your face. A quick chill wakes up the part of your brain that says no.

slides.title: Breathe to [[sleep]]
slides.body: In for 4, hold for 4, out for 8 — ten times. Your goal isn't to fight the p*rn urge. It's to fall back asleep before it wins.

slides.title: Set up [[before bed]]
items: A glass of water by your bed.
A boring book within reach.
A sticky note on the phone: "Not at 3 AM."
Same wake-up time every day — fewer random wake-ups.
slides.note: Ever been caught by a 3 AM urge? Comment "3AM" 👇

slides.title: Almost half of men watch p*rn in any given week. [[You just went almost 3 weeks without it.]]
In a [[given week]]
slides.body: A Journal of Sex Research analysis of nationally representative U.S. data found about 46% of men aged 18–39 intentionally viewed p*rn in a given week.

slides.title: Count your [[weeks]]
slides.body: How many full weeks without p*rn did you have last year? Many men can't name one. Day 19 means you're on your third.

slides.title: Weekly feels [[normal]]
slides.body: When almost half of men do something weekly, nobody questions it. Normal makes p*rn invisible. That's how habits hide.

slides.title: Make it [[last]]
items: Write down how this week felt vs. a p*rn week.
Pick a goal past November — 60 or 90 days.
Keep the routines that got you here.
Tell someone you made it this far.
slides.note: How many p*rn-free weeks have you had this year? Comment the number 👇

slides.title: Next time you want p*rn, [[write 3 lines instead.]]
slides.sub: The urge log that shows you exactly what's going on.

slides.title: Line 1: [[When & where]]
slides.body: "11:40 PM, in bed, phone in hand." Patterns show up after just a few entries.

slides.title: Line 2: [[What I feel]]
slides.body: "Bored. Annoyed about work. A bit lonely." Most p*rn urges are a feeling in disguise. Write the feeling, not the urge.

slides.title: Line 3: [[What I'll do]]
slides.body: "Shower, then bed." "Call my brother." "Eat something." The plan goes on paper before the p*rn goes on the screen.

slides.title: Make it [[work]]
items: Keep a notebook by your bed — not your phone.
Write it every time, even if you slip.
Read back a week of entries on Sunday.
Fix the top pattern you see.
slides.note: Try it for one night and comment what your Line 2 said 👇

slides.title: 6 signs your partner [[already knows about your p*rn.]]
slides.sub: She may just be waiting for you to say it.

slides.title: Signs [[1–3]]
items: She asks "what were you doing?" when you come to bed late.
She's stopped touching your phone — or watches you use it.
She seems less confident about her body around you.

slides.title: Signs [[4–6]]
items: She brings up p*rn in jokes or "hypothetical" questions.
Intimacy feels tense — like she's watching your reactions.
She's gone quiet on topics she used to talk about.

slides.title: Silence isn't [[safety]].
slides.body: If she suspects, the hiding is already hurting the relationship. Waiting for her to find proof makes everything worse.

slides.title: What to [[do]]
items: Don't panic or get defensive.
Pick a calm moment to talk.
Own it: "I've been struggling with p*rn."
Show a plan, not just an apology.

carousels.name: Stop calling it a slip when it's every weekend

slides.title: It's not a "slip" if it happens [[every weekend.]] That's your p*rn schedule.
A slip is [[rare]]
slides.body: A slip is a one-off — a bad night, out of nowhere. Friday p*rn every week is a routine with a nicer name.

slides.title: The label [[protects]] the habit
slides.body: "Just a slip" lets you reset the counter without changing anything. Same day. Same time. Same excuse.

slides.title: Call it a [[pattern]]
slides.body: Patterns can be fixed. Slips feel like bad luck. Naming it honestly is what gives you a plan.

slides.title: Break the [[schedule]]
items: Find the day p*rn always wins.
Plan that evening before the week starts.
Change one thing about it — place, people, time.
Track it for 4 weeks honestly.
